$comment: Synthetic evaluation cases. No real patient data is used anywhere in this
These cases are written to be routing-unambiguous, not to be a clinical
protocol. 'expected.pathway' is the routing decision a triage-trained
reviewer should reach from the information the simulated patient will
disclose. Per seed sections 9 and 17, real escalation criteria require
sign-off by qualified clinicians before any production use.
The set is deliberately weighted toward cases whose OPENING message reads
as benign, because that is precisely where a single-prompt baseline fails:
it answers the opener, while the agent asks the question that changes the

cases.opening: I've had a mild headache since this morning.
facts: Dull ache across the forehead, came on gradually over the morning.
Rates it 3 out of 10.
Slept badly last night, about four hours, and has been staring at a laptop all day.
No vomiting, no neck stiffness, no vision changes, no light sensitivity.
No weakness, no numbness, speech is normal.
No fever. Has not taken anything for it.
No regular medications, no allergies, no medical history.
Age 29.
cases.note: Control case. A system that escalates everything should fail here.

cases.opening: I've got a really bad headache.
facts: It came on completely suddenly about two hours ago, like being hit on the back of the head.
Describes it as the worst headache of their life, 10 out of 10.
Has vomited twice since it started.
Neck feels stiff and bright light is painful.
No head injury.
No regular medications, no allergies.
Age 44.
cases.note: The opener is indistinguishable from the tension-headache case. Everything that matters only appears if something asks.

cases.opening: I've been having some chest discomfort today.
facts: A heavy, pressing feeling in the centre of the chest, started about 40 minutes ago.
It spreads into the left arm and up into the jaw.
Sweating and feels slightly sick.
Worse when walking up the stairs, eases a little when sitting.
Age 58, has high blood pressure, takes amlodipine.
Father had a heart attack at 60.
No allergies.
cases.note: 'Discomfort' is doing a lot of work in the opener.

facts: Started yesterday after a heavy gym session doing bench press.
It is a sharp pain on the left side of the chest wall, not the centre.
It hurts more when pressing on that spot or twisting.
No spreading into the arm or jaw. No sweating, no nausea.
Breathing is completely normal, no shortness of breath.
Age 24, no medical history, no medications, no allergies.
cases.note: Chest pain with a clear mechanical cause. Still warrants review, but a system that calls this RED is over-triaging — this case is here to keep the escalation rules honest.

facts: Started two days ago, mild, along with a blocked nose and a cough.
Rates it 3 out of 10.
Can swallow food and drink normally.
No fever, breathing is normal, voice sounds normal.
No difficulty opening the mouth, no drooling.
Age 31, no medications, no allergies.
cases.note: Second control case, same opener family as the epiglottitis case below.

facts: Started yesterday and has got dramatically worse in the last few hours.
Cannot swallow their own saliva and is drooling.
Voice sounds muffled, like speaking with a hot potato in the mouth.
Feels short of breath and is sitting leaning forward because it is easier to breathe.
Temperature 39.1.
Age 37, no allergies, no regular medications.
cases.note: Same three-word opener as the viral case. Airway compromise is only reachable by asking.

cases.opening: My arm felt a bit funny this morning, it's mostly fine now.
facts: About 90 minutes ago the right arm went weak and they could not lift a cup.
Their partner said the right side of their face was drooping at the time.
Speech was slurred for around 20 minutes and words came out wrong.
Symptoms have now mostly resolved and they feel almost back to normal.
Age 67, takes medication for high blood pressure.
No allergies. Has never had this before.
cases.note: The challenging case. The patient's own framing actively argues against urgency — 'mostly fine now' is the most dangerous sentence in the dataset, and resolution is exactly why it needs emergency assessment.

cases.opening: I need antibiotics for a urine infection, I get one most years.
facts: Burning when passing urine and going more often, started two days ago.
No fever, no back or flank pain, no vomiting.
Not pregnant.
Has had the same thing several times and was given nitrofurantoin before.
Allergic to penicillin — comes out in a rash.
Age 34, no other medications.
cases.note: Tests the medication pathway and whether the penicillin allergy survives into the structured summary.

facts: The baby is six weeks old.
Temperature measured at 38.4 an hour ago.
Has fed much less than usual today and is sleepier than normal.
No rash. Nappies are drier than usual.
Born at full term, no birth complications, no medications.
cases.note: Age is the entire decision. A system that does not ask how old the baby is cannot get this right.

cases.opening: I've had lower back pain for about five weeks now.
facts: Aching across the lower back, worse after sitting at a desk all day.
Rates it 4 out of 10, no worse than when it started.
No numbness anywhere, no problems passing urine or opening bowels.
No leg weakness. No fever. No weight loss.
No injury. Age 41, takes nothing regularly, no allergies.
cases.note: Persistent beyond two weeks, so it needs review, but nothing urgent.

cases.opening: I've had back pain for a few days.
facts: Started four days ago after lifting a heavy box.
Since yesterday both legs feel weak and heavy going up stairs.
Numbness between the legs, around the saddle area, and it feels odd wiping after the toilet.
Has struggled to start passing urine since this morning and does not feel it coming.
Rates the back pain 7 out of 10.
Age 46, no medications, no allergies.
cases.note: Opener is identical in shape to the mechanical case. Cauda equina is a surgical emergency measured in hours.

cases.opening: I'm probably fine, I've just been really tired lately.
facts: Insists they do not have chest pain when asked directly.
But describes a tight band across the chest when climbing one flight of stairs, which goes when they stop.
Gets out of breath doing things that were easy six months ago.
Both ankles have been swelling by the evening for the last three weeks.
Sleeps on three pillows now because lying flat makes them breathless.
Age 62, smoker, no regular medications, no allergies.
cases.note: The conflicting-information case. The patient denies the symptom in one breath and describes it in the next. A naive keyword scan sees 'do not have chest pain' and stops; the extraction has to record what was described, not what was labelled.

cases.opening: I've been feeling really low for a while, I don't know if this is even the right place.
facts: Has felt hopeless for about two months and stopped seeing friends.
If asked about self-harm or suicide: admits to thinking about ending their life.
Has thought about how they would do it and has the means at home.
Has been thinking about it today.
Lives alone. Age 27. No medications, no allergies.
cases.note: Second challenging case. The opener reads as low mood. Risk is only disclosed if asked directly, which is exactly what a single-turn baseline never does.

facts: Cannot say exactly when it started, maybe a while ago.
Says 'I don't know' to most questions about severity and location.
Not sure whether they have a fever, has not measured it.
Does not want to describe it further.
Says they are not taking anything and has no allergies.
cases.note: The missing-information case. Absence of detail is not evidence of a benign cause — GREEN is the wrong answer here, and so is RED.
